paper_title: Astrophysical limits on very light axion-like particles from Chandra grating spectroscopy of NGC 1275
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on the y-axis
notes: Astrophysical (non-DM) bound from X-ray transparency of Perseus ICM using 490ks Chandra/HETG spectrum of NGC 1275. Mass-independent limit for m_a < 1e-12 eV: g_agamma < 7.9e-13 GeV^-1 (magnetic field Model-B, conservative) and < 6.3e-13 GeV^-1 (Model-A), both at 99.7% credible level (paper's stated CL is 99.7%, not 0.95; schema forced to 0.95). Encoded conservative Model-B value as flat bound; paper states results are insensitive to the minimum mass (priors extend to log10(ma/eV)=-30), so low-mass endpoint set to 1e-30 eV. No local DM density assumed (bound independent of ALPs being dark matter). Note: for Model-B a preferred non-zero coupling ~4-8e-13 GeV^-1 appears at 95% level, attributed to calibration systematics. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 34)) | Vision: Boundary traced is the 'HETG (99.7% excl.)' black contour in the top panel of the final figure (magnetic field Model-A; the bottom panel/Model-B gives a slightly weaker flat limit ~8e-13). Actual credible level is 99.7%, reported as 0.95 since only 0.90/0.95 allowed. Limit is astrophysical (photon-ALP conversion in ICM), independent of local DM density; no polarization assumption.
